extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers conducting or using reliability/validation studies of clinical, behavioral, or observational measurement tools
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical findings about how to evaluate and improve interrater/intrarater reliability and other psychometric properties of clinical and observational instruments (including which statistics to use, training/calibration practices, and interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability and diagnostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare interrater reliability and overall diagnostic accuracy between rater groups (e.g., experienced vs neophyte interviewers) and track maintenance of reliability over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experienced interviewers may achieve better reliability and diagnostic accuracy, but with standardized training and quality assurance procedures both experienced and inexperienced raters can attain and maintain high levels. Perform a quality-assurance check after training to detect remaining differences and standardize training/QA across sites to improve comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-interval test-retest interrater reliability (accounting for variance sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a test-retest approach to assess interrater reliability, account for rater variance in elicitation and interpretation and patient variance across interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish base-rate requirements before calculating reliability coefficients; explicitly model the three sources of variance (rater elicitation, rater interpretation, patient change) to avoid biased estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronbach's alpha (internal consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cronbach's alpha to assess internal consistency of multi-item scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alpha with confidence intervals when possible. Large ranges (e.g., .81-.96) indicate good to excellent internal consistency; interpret in context of scale length and dimensionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split-half reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess internal consistency via split-half correlations as an adjunct to Cronbach's alpha.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report split-half reliability (and method used to split) alongside alpha to support internal consistency claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stability of measurements over time by repeating assessments after a short interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report test-retest correlation (and time interval). Use for measures intended to capture stable traits; ensure interval short enough to limit true change but long enough to avoid recall bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa / weighted kappa (categorical agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use kappa statistics to quantify agreement for categorical diagnoses or classifications beyond chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa with confidence intervals and interpret using conventional bands (e.g., 0.41-0.60 moderate; 0.61-0.80 substantial). Use weighted kappa for ordinal categories. Note kappa can be affected by base rates; consider complementary metrics (percent agreement, prevalence-adjusted measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to quantify agreement for continuous or ordinal scores among raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the ICC model/type (e.g., two-way random), ICC value with 95% CI, and interpret magnitude. For numerical variables ICC may be preferable to percent agreement; use ICC for interrater and intrarater reliability of scale scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Krippendorff's alpha for measuring agreement across multiple raters and variable types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate when varying numbers of raters or missing data are present; report with CI and consider alongside other agreement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement / inter-observer agreement (IOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw percent agreement or IOA as a descriptive indicator of rater concordance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful complementary statistic to kappa/ICC; high IOA coupled with high kappa/ICC gives stronger evidence of agreement. IOA > .87 and ICCs > .91 have been reported as excellent in observational fieldwork contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal detectable change (MDC) and MDC%
rubrics_metrics.description: Report MDC and MDC% to quantify random measurement error and the smallest change beyond measurement noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MDC and MDC% alongside ICC to contextualize reliability for outcome measurement; use MDC% to compare measurement error across instruments or populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and cut-off selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When instruments use thresholds (cut-offs) for case classification, evaluate diagnostic performance using sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select cut-offs based on criterion validity analyses and report sensitivity/specificity and PPV/NPV for chosen thresholds. Discuss context-dependent properties (e.g., cognitive impairment affecting D-scale reliability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive validity and ROC/C-statistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess an instrument's ability to predict relevant outcomes using predictive validity measures and ROC/AUC analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report C-statistic/AUC with confidence intervals and interpret in clinical context (e.g., C = 0.82 indicates good discriminatory ability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor analysis / construct validity (exploratory/confirmatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use factor analysis to examine scale dimensionality and support construct validity (e.g., identify components such as 'anger' and 'psychomotor excitation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report factor loadings, variance explained, and fit statistics when conducting confirmatory factor analysis; use results to inform scoring and subscale interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database quality metrics: completeness, consistency, and interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate registry/database quality using completeness, consistency, and interrater reliability metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness and consistency alone may not reflect true data quality; interrater reliability (Cohen's kappa, ICC) better identifies unreliable specific variables. For audits, apply completeness/consistency to full dataset and interrater reliability on a randomized subset with direct auditing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use majority voting and multi-rater agreement statistics for consensus labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: For visual/subjective event labelling, use majority voting to assign consensus labels and quantify agreement with Fleiss' kappa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportions of high/moderate/poor agreement and examine how event characteristics (duration, amplitude) and database composition influence agreement. Majority voting can highlight which events are robustly labelled versus ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training, calibration, and baseline reliability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide standardized training and conduct baseline interrater reliability checks before implementing competency evaluations or routine scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline reliability data are needed prior to integrating evaluations into programs. Training can improve reliability for specific subscales/items; run post-training QA checks and consider multiple training sessions where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use same raters across repeated measurements when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce random measurement error across time, prefer using the same rater(s) for longitudinal outcome assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different raters are used, anticipate greater random error and report interrater reliability; when using different raters, interpret change scores cautiously and consider adjusting sample size or analysis methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer objective or low-discretion measures for higher reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures that require less subjective rater judgement tend to exhibit higher interrater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rating items to be concrete and observable (e.g., presence of password protection) if consistent scoring is desired. Clinical-quality or usability judgments may have poor reliability and require clearer operational definitions or multiple raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report confidence intervals and sample characteristics for reliability estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 95% confidence intervals and describe rater experience, number of raters, sample size, and case-mix when reporting reliability statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence intervals and sample/context details help assess precision and generalizability of reliability estimates (e.g., ICC .85, 95% CI x–y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret kappa/statistic magnitudes using conventional bands and statistical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify kappa values into interpretive bands (e.g., moderate, substantial) and test whether values differ from zero or across conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established interpretation ranges (paper example: moderate 0.41–0.60; substantial 0.61–0.80). Test pre-post training differences and between-standards differences for statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess item- and subscale-level reliability and revise low-reliability items
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine reliability at the item and subscale level to identify problematic questions or domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-reliability items (e.g., two physical environment items with low Kappa) should be reworded or reconsidered; instrument manuals may require revision to improve scoring clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for rater experience and stratify or adjust analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rater background, experience, and training level influence reliability; consider stratified analyses or targeted training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report interrater reliability by rater experience groups (professionals vs parents, trained vs untrained) as reliability may vary substantially; targeted training for inexperienced raters can markedly improve agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-rate and sample composition considerations before computing reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful that low or extreme base rates for categories and case-mix can affect reliability statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform and report base-rate analyses and consider prevalence-adjusted metrics or complementary statistics (percent agreement, ICC) when base rates are extreme. Database composition can materially influence agreement patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select statistical metric appropriate to variable type
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose agreement statistics that match the measurement level: ICC for numeric/continuous, kappa for categorical/ordinal, Krippendorff's alpha for multiple raters/variable types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using inappropriate metrics can misrepresent reliability (e.g., use ICC rather than percent agreement for numeric variables; state the specific ICC model used).
